name: George Colman the Younger
credit: George Colman the Younger, engraving by William Ridley and Blood, 1809 · Public domain (Wikimedia Commons)
bio: George Colman the Younger (1762–1836) was an English dramatist and humorous poet, author of the comedies The Heir at Law and John Bull. He later served as Examiner of Plays, and his comic verse was collected in Broad Grins (1802) and My Night-Gown and Slippers (1797).

The poem here is the one printed under his name in Frederick Locker's Lyra Elegantiarum (London: E. Moxon, 1867), an anthology of vers de société and vers d'occasion by deceased authors; the texts follow that first edition.

poems.title: My muse and I, ere youth and spirits fled
poems.author: George Colman the Younger
poems.collection: Lyra Elegantiarum, ed. Frederick Locker (London: E. Moxon, 1867)
poems.text:
My muse and I, ere youth and spirits fled.
Sat up together many a night, no doubt:
But now I've sent the poor old lass to bed,
Simply because my fire is going out.
